newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds surge, focus on the short end.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds surge, focus on the short end.

text.p: Irish government bonds continued their upward momentum in very heavy trade on Friday as domestic and foreign investors pumped further cash into the market.

"The Dublin market has been trading in very high volumes over the last few days. The strong Irish pound performance on ERM crosses is helping the market. The curve has steepened and we're seeing some focus on the front end of the market," one dealer said.
By 1520 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was up 66p at 106.06 to yield 6.17 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was up 40p at 107.00 to yield 6.87 percent.
The spread against German Bunds in the 10-year area of the curve fell to a new recent low of 90 basis points after spending the week hovering around the 100 basis points level.
Dealers said the market would focus on end-August banking data next week. The central bank is due to release the figures on Thursday.

"The first credit data in a higher interest rate environment will be the September credit data because the central bank raised rates in early August and the institutions raised them in late August. For this reason August's credit figures will have limited relevance for the market," the dealer said.
